gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

Two problems block merging, and the repair stopped because its last attempts on the export problem made no progress.

1. The import accepts a CSV file with no header row, so a file missing its column names still loads. The test "requires header" in test/import.test.js covers this case (src/import.js:41).

Problem 2

### What is blocked

The CSV export drops any row whose name contains a comma, so a list with three people comes out with two rows (src/export.js:31). The test "exports quoted names" in test/export.test.js fails with: expected 3 rows, got 2.

### Why the repair stopped

The repair changed how the export puts quote marks around names, twice. Each time the test still failed with "expected 3 rows, got 2", and the repair undid its own edits. Why the row goes missing is still unknown, so another attempt would repeat the same guess.

### What you can do

- deliver: continues the repair work, but tries this problem again only after something about its failure changes, such as a new commit or a clue to the cause.
- assess: posts both problems on the PR as a review and repairs nothing.
- stop: removes the local checkout and leaves the PR as it is.
- overrule 2: sets this problem aside for this run; problem 1 still blocks merging.

I recommend stop because no other choice can change the outcome until the cause of the lost row is known.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the local checkout and leave the PR and its branch as they are. [recommended]
2. deliver - continue the repair with more repair and sync attempts added; it retries the export problem only after its failure changes.
3. assess - post both problems to the PR as a review and make no repairs.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: All three facts moved from fails to holds, and Before held none of them, so nothing regressed. What moved them: After gives each attempted blocker a "Problem n" label followed by the three ### headings, with locators, the quoted failure and an explicit "cause is unknown". It keeps A's unattempted problem 1 as a short numbered item ahead of the sectioned problem 2. It adds a per-action "What you can do" list carrying "overrule 2" in A, "overrule 1" in B, and the check dispositions with no overrule in C. Before rendered plain paragraphs with no headings and no overrule at all. Three things are fragile and worth tightening. First, each stuck block is under 180 words only if counted through the last "What you can do" bullet (about 164, 146 and 140 words); the recommendation and the "Pick one" list restate deliver, assess and stop, so a reader who counts those lines would see the limit broken and each action listed twice. Say explicitly that the block ends at the last bullet, or have the numbered menu not repeat the consequences. Second, B's deliver is worded as "continues the delivery work" without the changed-input condition, although the exhausted problem is the sole blocker; state that deliver is a retry only after the failure input changes, as A and C do. Third, C adds consequences for flaky, real and ci-broken that the supplied results do not state, and A's problem 1 no longer says that no repair was attempted, which Before did; restrict the wording to supplied facts and keep the unattempted status in the short item.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: All three facts moved from fails to holds, as the Change intended, and Before held none of them, so nothing was lost. Before rendered every attempted finding as plain prose with no Problem n or three ### sections, and offered neither overrule in A and B nor the check command as a listed choice in C. After adds Problem n with What is blocked, Why the repair stopped and What you can do, keeps the file and test locators, quotes the failed output, and says the lost row's cause is unknown without inventing one. It keeps A's unattempted problem 1 as a short numbered item ahead of the stuck problem 2, lists overrule 2 and overrule 1 with consequences, gives C the check test flaky | real | ci-broken command with no overrule, and puts a one-sentence recommendation above Pick one with no merge or reject. Two things are worth pinning down in the wording so these stay held. First, state that the 180-word limit covers the three sections only: each block is roughly 110 words on that reading, but about 200 if the recommendation and Pick one list are counted, because deliver, assess and stop appear both as bullets and as numbered picks. Either say the bullets and the menu are separate, or have the bullets carry only the finding's own command. Second, say whether Problem n is itself a heading or a plain label, and keep the explicit sentence that adding run attempts does not reopen an exhausted repair.
